recentMonths.summary: Completed multiple iterations of FB_MotorControl development: first delivered a full industrial motor control PLC project with structured+OOP hybrid architecture meeting SIL2 safety standards and <100ms response time; then developed an advanced OOP-based FB_MotorControl with enhanced requirements including 0-100% analog speed regulation, multi-channel fault protection, diagnostic logging, <10ms response time, and 1ms cycle support; delivered an enhanced solution with full functional and performance-optimized versions achieving single-cycle execution time <0.2ms, response time 1.2-1.8ms, and fault detection time <0.1ms; confirmed validation passed and finalized project delivery with verification report. Most recently, completed a comprehensive FB_MotorControl development project including requirement analysis, OOP architecture design with custom base classes, implementation of core control logic, multi-channel protection, diagnostic capabilities, creation of a dedicated ramp generator function block, full TwinCAT validation and compliance fixes, performance optimization to support 1ms cycles, and delivery of complete documentation alongside all code files, resulting in a fully validated, production-ready solution with 9 deliverable files. Has now completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block for automated cotton candy machine control, which activates the sugar feeder when sugar level is below 10.0 units and sets motor speed to positive input values or 0 for non-positive inputs. The cotton candy machine control solution underwent full validation with a 92/100 health score, passed all 5 formal property checks, and was optimized with improved variable naming (MotorSpeed renamed to SpinningMotorSpeed). Has also completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block AutomaticDoorControl.TcPOU for a retail environment automatic door control system, which controls door state based on proximity sensor input and elapsed time since last opening, with a 5000ms open duration constant; the solution passed all 4 formal property checks, fully complies with TwinCAT syntax specifications, and has no syntax errors or redundant code. Additionally, has completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block WastewaterControl for a wastewater treatment plant, which controls two pumps and two valves based on inlet flow rate, outlet flow rate, pH level, and tank level inputs with threshold-based logic, featuring input boundary handling (InFlow/OutFlow: 0.0~1000.0 m³/h, pH: 0.0~14.0, TankLvl: 0.0~100.0%), centralized constant management, and full TwinCAT compliance with a 98/100 health score and passing all 4 formal property checks. Has also completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_BookSorting for an automated library book sorting system, which controls a conveyor motor and three sorting bins using input from three RFID readers, with logic ensuring only one bin is open at a time, motor activation tied to any RFID detection, and all outputs updated based on end-of-cycle RFID readings; delivered two optimized versions (basic and edge detection) alongside supporting global variable table and main program files. Has completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_FlowerArrangement for an automatic flower arranging machine, which controls an arranging mechanism (output values 0-4) and conveyor belt based on flower type (1-2) and color (1-2) sensor inputs with specified combination logic, including input range validation and CASE statement-based branch logic, and passed all 5 formal property checks. Has completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block HomeBrewingSystem for a home brewing system, which controls a heating element, agitation motor, hops dispenser, and fermentation tank based on temperature (below 65.0°C activates heating), water flow (above 0.5 units activates agitation), and brewing time (after 5 hours activates hops dispenser, after 48 hours activates fermentation tank), featuring input validity checks and safety state management, passing all 6 formal property checks with a 95/100 health score and full TwinCAT compliance. Has initiated four other new projects: developing a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block for a smart irrigation system that controls a water pump based on dual soil moisture sensor readings (REAL values) and weather forecast inputs (integer: 0=sunny, 1=rainy, 2=cloudy) with specific activation/deactivation logic; developing a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_BreakerControlSystem to manage 7 power system breakers with open/close/trip functionality and calculated output points based on breaker states; developing a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_CircuitControl to manage a power distribution system with specified inputs, outputs, internal variables, and short circuit detection logic requirements; developing an AdvancedCircuitBreakerControlFB Structured Text (ST) PLC function block for a circuit breaker control system with a stable-state initialization loop and state machine transitions through defined states based on input conditions. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block DocumentFilingSystem for an automatic document filing system, which controls a conveyor motor and four storage bins based on document detection (DocumentInlet: BOOL) and category selection (CategorySelector: INT) inputs; the solution implements a 4-state machine architecture (standby→transfer→wait for bin entry→entry complete), includes dual safety mutual exclusion, timer management (5-second transfer, 2-second wait, 3-second bin opening), input validation for category values 1-4, and automatic reset functionality, achieving a 95/100 health score, passing all formal property checks, and fully complying with TwinCAT specifications. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block MuseumClimateControl for a museum climate control system, which controls HVAC, humidifier, dehumidifier, and lighting systems based on humidity (HumiditySensor: REAL), temperature (TemperatureSensor: REAL), and light level (LightSensor: BOOL) inputs; the solution implements hysteresis control (humidity ±2%RH, temperature ±0.5°C), safety mutual exclusion to prevent simultaneous humidifier/dehumidifier operation, output initialization, and optimized logic, achieving a 95/100 health score and full compliance with TwinCAT specifications. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block ChargingStationControl for an electric vehicle charging station, which controls charging activation based on EV connection status, battery voltage (threshold > MinimumVoltage), charging current (limit ≤ MaximumCurrent), state of charge (<100.0%), and charging timer (≤ MaximumChargingTime) inputs with specified threshold logic; the solution includes charging stop conditions for any violated startup criteria, internal TON timer for charging time accumulation, fault diagnostic outputs (fault flag + fault code), passed all relevant validation checks, achieved a 98/100 health score, and is fully compliant with TwinCAT 3.1.4024 specifications. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block GreenhouseWateringSystem for an automatic greenhouse watering system, which controls sprinkler activation based on soil moisture levels (engages when below 30%, disengages when above 70%), includes a 5-second system response delay to prevent frequent cycling, input validation to ensure moisture readings stay within 0-100% range, maintains initial sprinkler off state, and passed all 5 formal property checks with a 98/100 health score and full TwinCAT compliance. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block RoboticArmColorSorting for a color-sorting robotic arm, which controls arm movement and bin activation based on red, green, blue color sensor inputs; the solution ensures arm activation when any color sensor detects a color, arm stop when no colors are detected, exclusive activation of only one bin at a time, red bin activation solely dependent on red sensor detection, passed all 4 formal property checks, and is fully compliant with TwinCAT specifications, delivered alongside a detailed design document. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block CoffeeMachineControl for a coffee machine, which controls water heating, grinder operation, and brewing processes based on StartButton input and ElapsedTime (milliseconds) input, featuring sequential process logic (30-second water heating → 15-second grinding → 60-second brewing), mutual exclusion of concurrent processes, output status indicators, time overflow protection, and compliance with TwinCAT specifications; the solution passed all 5 formal property checks, achieved a 98/100 health score, and includes optimized variable naming and detailed state machine comments. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_SimpleCalculation, which implements two loop calculation logics: assigning INPUT_VAR1 (initialized to 2) to OUTPUT_VAR1 and multiplying by 2 for 5 iterations, and assigning VAR2 (initialized to 0) to OUTPUT_VAR2 and incrementing by 1 for 5 iterations; the solution passed all 3 formal property checks, achieved a 100/100 health score, and is fully compliant with TwinCAT specifications. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_PointOperations and associated POINT data type, which defines a POINT structure with X and Y integer fields, creates a function block with INPUT_VAR2 (INT, default 7), internal variable VAR2, and outputs OUTPUT_VAR1 (POINT), OUTPUT_VAR2 (INT), OUTPUT_VAR3 (POINT), implementing logic to assign INPUT_VAR2 to VAR2 and OUTPUT_VAR2, set OUTPUT_VAR1 to (1,2), and set OUTPUT_VAR3 to (100, -7000), with 5 formal property ASSERT statements to validate all output values. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_RealValueAdjuster, which processes a real input value with multiple conditional adjustments: adds 1.0 when input is exactly 0.0, adds 1.0 when input is non-zero, adds 1.0 when integer conversion of input is non-zero, resulting in cumulative adjustments (0.0 input becomes 3.0, -1.0 input becomes 0.0, other non-zero values get +2.0), featuring floating-point tolerance comparison to avoid precision issues, formal validation assertions, and full compliance with TwinCAT specifications. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_SolarTracker for a solar panel tracking control system, which adjusts panel angles based on time of day (sunrise at 6 AM, sunset at 6 PM) and solar intensity levels; the solution sets panel angle to 0° during nighttime or outside operational hours, uses 30° for morning (6 AM-12 PM) and afternoon (12 PM-6 PM) periods, switches to 60° noon angle when solar intensity is ≥90% within a 30-minute window around noon, and ensures all output angles are limited to 0-90°; the solution passed all 7 formal property checks and is fully compliant with TwinCAT specifications. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block WindTurbineControl for a wind turbine control system, which adjusts blade pitch (INT, degrees) and generator speed (REAL, RPM) based on three wind speed categories: low (<=3.0) sets BladePitch to -5° and GeneratorSpeed to 500 RPM; moderate (>3.0 and <=5.0) sets BladePitch to 0° and GeneratorSpeed to 800 RPM; high (>5.0) sets BladePitch to 5° and GeneratorSpeed to 1000 RPM, with inputs including WindSpeedSensor (REAL) and GeneratorSpeedSensor (REAL), passing all 7 formal property checks with a 100/100 health score and fully compliant with TwinCAT specifications. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block SmartHVACSystem for a smart HVAC system, which monitors and sanitizes temperature/humidity sensor inputs, determines heating/cooling/ventilation requirements with heating/cooling priority over ventilation, controls HVAC operating mode (0=off, 1=cooling, 2=heating, 3=ventilation) and fan speed (0=off, 1=low, 2=medium, 3=high), and includes formal property validation assertions; delivered alongside a design document and core function block code file. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block FB_ParkingGarageController for a multi-level car parking system, which manages up to 100 parking slots and two elevators, assigns Elevator 1 to slots 1-50 and Elevator 2 to slots 51-100, tracks elevator current/target positions and busy/idle statuses, features elevator movement logic with 1-unit position increments, passed all 10 formal property checks, achieved a 95/100 health score, and includes optimized initialization logic (using FIRST_CYCLE instead of NOT FIRST_CYCLE) to follow standard programming practices. Most recently, completed development of a Structured Text (ST) PLC function block TrafficManagementSystem for a smart road traffic management system, which monitors vehicle counts at four intersections, independently manages two pairs of intersections (1 vs 2, 3 vs 4), dynamically sets green lights for intersections with higher vehicle counts while ensuring opposing intersections maintain complementary red/green states, uses efficient direct assignment logic for real-time updates, and passes all required formal property checks.
